**(i)** A certain vaccine is administered to a group of persons. It is observed that 0.1% of all the persons who take the vaccine suffered from a side effect.

Using the Poisson distribution, find, to four decimal places, the probability that out of 1000 persons who take the vaccine,

Avec $p = 60/1000 = 0.06$ et $n = 10$, la probabilité de (e) vaut environ $6.8 \times 10^{-9}$, soit $0.0000$ à 4 décimales : le corrigé donne la valeur exacte et note que l'événement est pratiquement impossible. La partie (d) est donnée à 4 décimales (0.0168).
Question 3 (i) : 1000 personnes et 0.1 % donnent $\lambda = 1$ ; les valeurs de Poisson sont calculées exactement ($e^{-1}$), sans lecture de table.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) none will suffer from the side effect.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of persons suffering the side effect. The mean number is $\lambda = np = 1000 \times 0.001 = 1$, so $X \sim \text{Po}(1)$ with $P(X = r) = \dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^r}{r!} = \dfrac{e^{-1}}{r!}$.

$$P(X = 0) = e^{-1} = 0.36788\ldots$$

**$P(X = 0) = 0.3679$.**

**(ii)** Out of 1000 customers that visit a telephone booth, 60 buy credit cards. Given that the number of customers buying credit follows a binomial distribution, find, the probability that in a randomly selected sample of 10 customers,

(d) exactly three buy credit cards
questions.corrige_markdown:
The probability that one customer buys credit is $p = \dfrac{60}{1000} = 0.06$. Let $Y$ be the number among 10 customers who buy credit: $Y \sim B(n = 10,\ p = 0.06)$, with $P(Y = r) = \dbinom{10}{r} (0.06)^r (0.94)^{10-r}$.

$$P(Y = 3) = \binom{10}{3}(0.06)^3(0.94)^7 = 120 \times 0.000216 \times 0.64848 = 0.01681\ldots$$

**$P(Y = 3) \approx 0.0168$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (e) more than seven buy credit cards
questions.corrige_markdown:
$$P(Y > 7) = P(Y = 8) + P(Y = 9) + P(Y = 10)$$

$$P(Y = 8) = \binom{10}{8}(0.06)^8(0.94)^2 = 45 \times 1.6796 \times 10^{-10} \times 0.8836 = 6.678 \times 10^{-9}$$

$$P(Y = 9) = 10\,(0.06)^9(0.94) = 9.47 \times 10^{-11}, \qquad P(Y = 10) = (0.06)^{10} = 6.05 \times 10^{-13}$$

$$P(Y > 7) \approx 6.77 \times 10^{-9}$$

**$P(Y > 7) \approx 6.8 \times 10^{-9}$**, which is $0.0000$ to four decimal places: with $p = 0.06$, more than seven buyers out of ten is practically impossible.
